    03 / FOLLOW YOUR APPETITE

    What to eat
    before you graduate.

    Start with a small plate. Learn a new name. Come back for your favourite.

    Open food checklist
    BENGALI CLASSICS

    More than just the sweets.

    Try fish preparations, kosha mangsho, luchi–aloo dum and shukto. Finish with mishti doi, sandesh, rosogolla (rasgulla) or payesh.

    Vegetarian starting points: luchi–aloo dum, sweets and vegetable dishes. Recipes vary: ask about fish, meat, egg, dairy and shared utensils rather than relying only on a dish’s name.

    KOLKATA STREET FOOD

    A city, one bite at a time.

    Kathi rolls, phuchka, jhal muri, ghugni, telebhaja, egg/chicken rolls, chowmein, momos, Kolkata biryani and roadside cha.

    These are things to look for, not claims that a particular stall is open. Ask the price first, choose busy stalls preparing food fresh and tell the vendor about dietary requirements.

    Kalyani first. Kolkata when you’re ready.

    Twelve named food leads across Kalyani, nearby Nadia and Kolkata. Start local, compare a real menu, and keep travel money separate.

    Price filters apply only to published example menu items, not complete meals or travel costs. Delivery prices can differ from counter prices and exclude extras. “Price unverified” preserves useful leads without pretending to know their menu. CHEAP refers only to the cited quick-bite price; MUST TRY is an editorial suggestion, not a rating.

    For the small-budget food hunt

    ₹50–₹100 TARGET

    Start with a single snack or tea. Confirm the total before ordering.

    ₹100–₹200 TARGET

    Choose a simple breakfast or roll; keep transport money separate.

    MID-RANGE PLAN

    ₹200–₹400 is a spending cap to discuss with a vendor, not a verified meal deal.

    SPECIAL OCCASION

    ₹400+ can go quickly at a café or sit-down restaurant. Read the menu first.

    Around JIS: ask seniors for their current breakfast, rice-meal, evening-snack and late dinner options. Check portions, kitchen hygiene, vegetarian preparation and whether the place serves at your actual class-break time. Unverified local restaurants are not presented as confirmed recommendations.

    04 / ENTER WITH RESPECT

    Temples, mosques
    & sacred places.

    Living places of faith first. Places to visit second. Read each field note for tradition, significance and etiquette.

    Visitor access is not the same as worship hours. Ask caretakers about entry, dress, footwear and photography. Never assume every space or ritual is open to visitors.

    Devotion & river-town culture

    Mayapur or Nabadwip. Choose one as the anchor; check road transfers and any ferry before combining them.

    Ballal Dhipi near Bamanpukur. Confirm public entry, travel in daylight and leave the fragile structures untouched.

    A longer nature day

    Bethuadahari needs an early start and current forest-access confirmation. Wildlife sightings are never promised.

    Krishnanagar Rajbari, Palashi and Ghurni are further research ideas named by the district tourism office; access, routes and hours need checking before they become a plan.

    08 / THE ACTUALLY USEFUL STUFF

    Hostel survival guide.

    Sort out the everyday things. Then the adventures get easier.

    These buttons open category searches around JIS; they are not endorsements or verified individual businesses. Check the exact pin, walking route, recent opening information and price before leaving. Start with hostel staff or seniors for the closest working option.

    Your first-week essentials run

    Food, groceries & drinking water

    Compare a simple meal at two nearby places, ask about vegetarian utensils and write down breakfast/dinner service times. Buy a reusable water bottle and keep a small shelf-stable snack in your room.

    Laundry, printing & stationery

    Ask whether laundry is per item or by weight, when it comes back, and how clothes are labelled. Before a deadline, test a local printing shop with one page and confirm paper sizes and opening hours.

    Banking, recharge, salons & gyms

    Use bank-marked ATMs; protect your PIN. Recharge through your operator’s official app or a known shop. Ask salons and gyms for a price list, trial access and cancellation terms before paying.

    Medical help, without guesswork

    Emergency in India: 112
    Police, fire and medical emergency coordination. Official ERSS source · Last verified: 1 October 2026.

    AIIMS Kalyani Trauma & Emergency:
    033-22027005

    For an urgent situation, call 112 and tell hostel staff your exact location. Do not delay help to compare map listings. The nearest suitable facility depends on the emergency.

    THE ART OF GETTING THERE & GETTING BACK

    How to escape the hostel.

    Decide your return first. The outward journey becomes much simpler.

    🚶 Nearby?

    Walk in daylight on suitable local roads, or ask for an e-rickshaw. Avoid using the expressway as a walking route.

    🛺 In town?

    Use local auto/e-rickshaw connections. Say the exact destination and agree shared/private fare and pickup point.

    🚆 Kolkata?

    Reach Kalyani station, confirm a Sealdah-bound train, then choose local public transport. Check the day’s Metro map and service notices.

    🚕 A group?

    Compare a live cab quote split by passengers with train plus local transport. Include tolls, waiting and the return journey.

    Kalyani main station or a branch-line stop?

    Kalyani main is the starting reference here. Silpanchal, Ghoshpara and Simanta are on the branch: the right station depends on your destination and current service. Ask hostel staff about the practical route from your gate. Naihati, Ranaghat, Dum Dum and Sealdah are useful railway hubs, but a train may not stop at every station.

    Buses & the last mile

    Ask staff or the conductor to confirm destination, stop and fare. Keep the destination written down. Do not treat a route number found on an old webpage as a guarantee of today’s service.

    Cycling

    Choose quiet, familiar roads and daylight, use a helmet and lights, and check secure parking. Avoid high-speed roads and unfamiliar routes during heavy rain.

    BEFORE YOU BOARD

    A return ticket is not a return plan.

    Check live running information, interchange time, the last practical connection and your hostel’s attendance rules. Keep a buffer for queues and missed trains. Buy a valid ticket through an official channel.

    Indian Railways NTES · Metro Railway Kolkata

    No current fares or departure times are quoted. The old official railway source supports the network only; check current services on your travel date. Source check: 1 October 2026.

    10 / GOOD COMPANY, GOOD PLACES

    Where to take your friends.

    For classmates, friends, couples or a small group. Choose the kind of time you want together.

    One plan everyone actually wants.

    Agree on budget and return time before you leave. Pick one anchor destination, one food stop and an optional extra. Meet at a clear public landmark if you split up.

    Quiet conversation: College Street browsing or a verified café. Sunset: a populated stretch at Prinsep Ghat. Fun: a shared market challenge or photo scavenger hunt; no unverified gaming venue is promised.

    SOLO EXPLORER

    Your own pace is a good pace.

    Begin with a daylight neighbourhood loop. Graduate to College Street bookstores, the Indian Museum, a confirmed café, a park or a respectful religious visit. Keep a first heritage walk short and on busy public streets.

    Tell someone where you are going, keep your phone charged, and check transport back before heading somewhere unfamiliar.

    YOUR PERSONAL FIELD LOG
    A new chapter
    12 / READ THE SEASON

    Bengal has more than one mood.

    🌸

    Winter

    Use cooler days for heritage walks, Nadia outings and longer photography sessions. Check attraction closures and carry a light layer.

    ☀️

    Summer

    Choose museums, shaded breaks and short morning outings. Carry water, avoid long exposed walks and check the day’s heat forecast.

    🌧

    Monsoon

    Keep plans flexible. Choose an indoor anchor, protect electronics, and avoid flooded lanes, slippery ghats and uncertain boat trips.

    🍂

    Festival season

    Allow more time for queues, traffic and rerouting. Go with a clear meeting point and a confirmed way back to Kalyani.

    FESTIVAL MODE

    When Kolkata
    changes character.

    Enjoy the art, food and shared streets without forgetting that these celebrations mean different things to different communities.

    Durga Puja · neighbourhoods become galleries

    Community pandals, worship and temporary artworks draw large crowds in Kolkata and across Bengal. Pick a small, current local circuit, queue patiently and never block rituals for photographs. Check police crowd and transport notices. West Bengal Tourism.

    Kali Puja · a devotional evening

    Local Kali temples and neighbourhood celebrations offer a way to observe respectfully. Follow queues and stay clear of fireworks. Late celebrations do not guarantee late trains or permission to return late to the hostel.

    Saraswati Puja · learning & community

    Look for permitted campus or neighbourhood celebrations. Accept invitations respectfully, ask before photographs and follow host rules. Confirm access with organisers rather than assuming a college event is public.

    Poila Boishakh · a Bengali new year

    Look for current cultural programmes and Bengali food offerings. Ask about event tickets and restaurant menus in advance; popular spots can be busy.

    Christmas · Park Street & churches

    Park Street’s festive atmosphere is a popular city experience. Separate a public street walk from church services: check service access and remain quiet during worship. Expect crowds, diversions and a slower journey home.

    Eid · celebration with respect

    Food and community gatherings may bring extra activity around neighbourhoods such as the Nakhoda area. Give worshippers space, ask before entering a mosque and confirm which food stalls are actually operating.

    Book fairs, film & cultural festivals

    Check the current organisers’ programmes for book fairs, film screenings, theatre and music. Dates, venues, passes and public access vary each year; do not travel using last year’s poster.

    No future festival dates are asserted here. Verify annual dates, local programmes, access and transport before travelling. Cultural overview sources checked 1 October 2026; current event arrangements remain unverified.

    Festival background and further reading
    13 / THE NON-NEGOTIABLES

    Smart explorer rules.

    A good story ends with getting back comfortably.

    Emergency · Call 112

    Before you leave

    • Tell someone your plan and keep emergency contacts.
    • Charge your phone; take some cash and keep return money aside.
    • Check closing times, access restrictions and the weather.
    • Check hostel rules and the last practical return connection.
    • For unfamiliar areas, consider taking a friend.

    While you are out

    • Avoid isolated areas after dark.
    • Use official or verified transport; confirm your destination.
    • Respect religious spaces, queues and photography rules.
    • Ask before photographing people and craftspeople.
    • Never assume the last train, bus or ferry is available.
    • Stay on public paths; keep away from unsafe river edges.

    112 is the Government of India’s emergency coordination number for police, fire and health assistance. Official source · Last verified: 1 October 2026.
